articles.content: Chennai TABLE TENNIS India U-19 boys win Bronze at ITTF World Youth Table Tennis Championships The Indian boys’ U-19 team bagged a bronze medal in the ITTF World Youth Table Tennis Championships in Istanbul on Tuesday. India blanked Turkey 3-0 in the quarterfinals to assure itself of a medal and then lost to Chinese Taipei 3-0 in the semifinals. The Results: Quarterfinal - India bt Turkey 3-0 (Priyanuj Bhattacharyya bt Kenen Kahraman 8-11, 11-8, 11-5; P. B. Abhinandh bt Berk Oztoprak 11-8, 6-11, 11-8, 11-6; R. Balamurugan bt Muhammet Atakul 8-11, 11-6, 11-9, 6-11, 11-8). Semifinal - Chinese Taipei bt India 3-0 (Chen-Yen Hung bt Priyanuj 9-11, 11-6, 7-11, 12-10, 12-10; Chin-Ting Lin bt P. B. Abhinandh 15-13, 11-4, 7-11, 11-7; Hao-Jen Yang bt R. Balamurugan 13-11, 11-9, 11-6). -Team Sportstar TENNIS International Lawn Tennis Club of India to celebrate 75th anniversary The International Lawn Tennis Club of India will celebrate its 75th anniversary by hosting a three-day international tennis gathering featuring players from 10 countries at the Delhi Gymkhana Club from November 27 to 29. The event will mark 75 years since India joined the World Council of the Club in 1951. Established in Great Britain in 1924, the 102-year-old International Lawn Tennis Club movement was founded with the idea of strengthening relations between countries through tennis. It now has a presence in 42 countries with around 4,500 members and follows the motto: “Handshakes across the net and friendship across the ocean.” The participating countries are Argentina, Barbados, Ireland, the United Kingdom, Norway, Sweden, Belgium, Slovenia, Australia and India. The participants include former players, with the tournament featuring two groups of five teams in a round-robin format, followed by the semifinals and final on November 29. Indian tennis legend and former Davis Cup player Ramesh Krishnan, a junior Wimbledon and French Open champion, will inaugurate the event. -PTI CHESS NODWIN Gaming to bring Gukesh-Sindarov World Championship clash closer to Indian fans NODWIN Gaming is set to support the Hindi broadcast of the FIDE World Championship 2026 between reigning World Champion D. Gukesh and Uzbekistan’s Javokhir Sindarov, beginning on Tuesday. Viewers in India will be able to follow the 14-game contest through a Hindi broadcast and a live viewing experience at Habitat, Mumbai. Alongside the broadcast, Habitat will host a live viewing experience where fans can follow the championship together, building on a similar gathering during the 2024 World Championship. The viewing experience will be streamed on NODWIN Gaming’s YouTube channel in association with Chess.com India, featuring commentary from Tania Sachdev, Amruta Mokal, Harshit Raja, Sahil Tickoo, Sahaj Grover and Sagar Shah. Gukesh, who became the 18th World Champion in 2024 at the age of 18 after defeating Ding Liren, will defend his title against Sindarov, who secured his place in the championship after winning the 2025 FIDE World Cup and the Candidates Tournament. The match will comprise up to 14 classical games, with the first player to reach 7.5 points claiming the title. -Team Sportstar GOLF HSBC Golf League Season 5 goes bigger with 18 events across 15 cities HSBC India today unveiled the fifth edition of the HSBC Golf League at the Bombay Presidency Golf Club in Mumbai, setting out its most ambitious calendar yet: 18 events across 15 cities up from 13 events across 11 cities last season. Former Indian cricketer Harbhajan Singh, 11-time Asian Tour winner Gaganjeet Bhullar, Asian Games gold medallist Pranavi Urs and Jaswinder Sodhi, HSBC India, unveiled Season 5 of the HSBC Golf League. Every round of this edition will build towards the finale, and the reward for the winner is a trip to Scotland for a hospitality experience of the 155th Open at St. Andrews between July 11 and 18 in 2027. “Sport has the power to inspire, unite and create opportunities. By combining our international scale with the passion of our customers, we aim to support the growth of golf, nurture young talent through grassroots initiatives and bring the excitement to wider audiences in India and beyond. Our ambition is to bring golf to more people across the world and to promote the game at all levels by inspiring future generations to take part in the sport. In Season 5, the HSBC Golf League will travel to more cities than ever before, culminating in a journey to the home of golf,” said Jaswinder Sodhi of HSBC India. This edition will be played in a stroke play format, with handicaps calculated using the Single Peoria system. All 18 events will be scored on the Golf League, the golf platform developed by HSBC India. -Team Sportstar MORE SPORTS Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championship starts in Mumbai The inaugural Youth Artistic Gymnastics National Championship commenced on Tuesday at INS Hamla, Malad, Mumbai. It is the first championship of its kind to be organised by a Services establishment. The week-long championship will bring together approximately 700 participants, including 219 women and 272 men competing in the championship, along with over 200 participants taking part in the trials. Addressing the participants, Rear Admiral R. K. Singh said, “Gymnastics and the Navy have a lot in common. Both demand discipline every single day, hours of practice that nobody sees, the courage to attempt what looks impossible and the composure to perform when it matters the most.” The championship comprises two disciplines: men’s Artistic Gymnastics (MAG) and women’s Artistic Gymnastics (WAG). The MAG competition has three grades: 7, 8 and 9. The WAG competition has grades 8, 9 and 10. Each grade is further divided into two categories: in-age-group and out-of-age-group. The MAG competition is being held from 24 to 26 November. Teams from 18 States and two Union Territories, along with SSCB, are taking part. These gymnasts will compete across six apparatus: floor exercise, pommel horse, still rings, vault, parallel bars and horizontal bar. These events test strength, balance, flexibility and coordination. The gymnasts are judged on the difficulty of their routines and their execution. The WAG competition will be held from 28 to 30 November. It will see participation from 17 States and two Union Territories. These gymnasts will compete across four apparatus: vault, uneven bars, balance beam and floor exercise. These events test strength, flexibility, balance and precision. Telangana and Haryana have fielded two teams each in both the men’s and women’s competitions. Selection trials for senior and junior men’s and women’s Artistic Gymnastics for the upcoming international championships will also be held at INS Hamla. The trials are scheduled for 27 November for MAG and 1 December 2026 for WAG. The championship will conclude on 30 November 2026. -Team Sportstar Hockey Punjab Hockey League: Roundglass Hockey Academy secures fourth win in a row to stay on top of the table Roundglass Hockey Academy made it four wins out of four matches while Odisha Naval Tata Hockey High Performance Centre secured a third-successive win with strong performances on day six of the Punjab Hockey League at the Olympian Balbir Singh Senior International Hockey Stadium. Roundglass Hockey Academy tightened its grip on the top spot with an emphatic 8-3 victory over Major Dhyanchand Sports College, Saifai, in a high-scoring encounter. The hosts were dominant through the match and scored at regular intervals to remove any doubt from the result of the match. In the final match of the day, Odisha Naval Tata Hockey HPC secured a clinical 3-1 victory over Naval Tata Hockey Academy, Jamshedpur. Following a tightly contested, goalless opening quarter, the Bhubaneswar outfit broke the deadlock in the 22nd minute to give it a 1-0 lead at half-time. articles.contentHindi: चेन्नई टेबल टेनिस भारत के अंडर-19 लड़कों ने आईटीटीएफ विश्व युवा टेबल टेनिस चैंपियनशिप में कांस्य पदक जीता। भारतीय लड़कों की अंडर-19 टीम ने मंगलवार को इस्तांबुल में आईटीटीएफ विश्व युवा टेबल टेनिस चैंपियनशिप में कांस्य पदक जीता। भारत ने क्वार्टर फाइनल में तुर्की को 3-0 से हराकर पदक पक्का कर लिया और फिर सेमीफाइनल में चीनी ताइपे से 3-0 से हार गया। परिणाम: क्वार्टरफ़ाइनल - भारत ने तुर्की को 3-0 से हराया (प्रियानुज भट्टाचार्य ने केनेन काहरमन को 8-11, 11-8, 11-5; पी. बी. अभिनंद ने बर्क ओज़्टोप्राक को 11-8, 6-11, 11-8, 11-6; आर. बालामुरुगन ने मुहम्मद अताकुल को 8-11, 11-6 से हराया। 11-9, 6-11, 11-8). सेमीफाइनल - चीनी ताइपे ने भारत को 3-0 से हराया (चेन-येन हंग ने प्रियानुज को 9-11, 11-6, 7-11, 12-10, 12-10; चिन-टिंग लिन ने पी.बी. अभिनंद को 15-13, 11-4, 7-11, 11-7; हाओ-जेन यांग ने आर. बालामुरुगन को हराया। 13-11, 11-9, 11-6). -टीम स्पोर्टस्टार टेनिस इंटरनेशनल लॉन टेनिस क्लब ऑफ इंडिया 75वीं वर्षगांठ मनाएगा। इंटरनेशनल लॉन टेनिस क्लब ऑफ इंडिया 27 से 29 नवंबर तक दिल्ली जिमखाना क्लब में 10 देशों के खिलाड़ियों की तीन दिवसीय अंतरराष्ट्रीय टेनिस सभा की मेजबानी करके अपनी 75वीं वर्षगांठ मनाएगा। यह आयोजन 1951 में भारत के क्लब की विश्व परिषद में शामिल होने के 75 साल पूरे होने पर मनाया जाएगा। 1924 में ग्रेट ब्रिटेन में स्थापित, 102 साल पुराने अंतर्राष्ट्रीय लॉन टेनिस क्लब आंदोलन की स्थापना टेनिस के माध्यम से देशों के बीच संबंधों को मजबूत करने के विचार से की गई थी। अब लगभग 4,500 सदस्यों के साथ इसकी 42 देशों में उपस्थिति है और यह आदर्श वाक्य का पालन करता है: "नेट के पार हाथ मिलाना और समुद्र के पार दोस्ती।" भाग लेने वाले देश अर्जेंटीना, बारबाडोस, आयरलैंड, यूनाइटेड किंगडम, नॉर्वे, स्वीडन, बेल्जियम, स्लोवेनिया, ऑस्ट्रेलिया और भारत हैं। प्रतिभागियों में पूर्व खिलाड़ी भी शामिल हैं, टूर्नामेंट में राउंड-रॉबिन प्रारूप में पांच टीमों के दो समूह होंगे, जिसके बाद 29 नवंबर को सेमीफाइनल और फाइनल होगा। भारतीय टेनिस के दिग्गज और पूर्व डेविस कप खिलाड़ी रमेश कृष्णन, जूनियर विंबलडन और फ्रेंच ओपन चैंपियन, इस कार्यक्रम का उद्घाटन करेंगे। -पीटीआई चेस नोडविन गेमिंग गुकेश-सिंदारोव विश्व चैम्पियनशिप मुकाबले को भारतीय प्रशंसकों के करीब लाएगा। नोडविन गेमिंग मौजूदा विश्व चैंपियन डी. गुकेश और उज्बेकिस्तान के जावोखिर सिंधारोव के बीच मंगलवार से शुरू होने वाली फिडे विश्व चैंपियनशिप 2026 के हिंदी प्रसारण का समर्थन करने के लिए तैयार है। भारत में दर्शक हिंदी प्रसारण और हैबिटेट, मुंबई में लाइव देखने के अनुभव के माध्यम से 14-गेम प्रतियोगिता का अनुसरण कर सकेंगे। प्रसारण के साथ-साथ, हैबिटेट एक लाइव देखने के अनुभव की मेजबानी करेगा जहां प्रशंसक 2024 विश्व चैंपियनशिप के दौरान इसी तरह की सभा का निर्माण करते हुए एक साथ चैंपियनशिप का अनुसरण कर सकते हैं। देखने का अनुभव Chess.com India के सहयोग से NODWIN गेमिंग के YouTube चैनल पर स्ट्रीम किया जाएगा, जिसमें तानिया सचदेव, अमृता मोकल, हर्षित राजा, साहिल टिक्कू, सहज ग्रोवर और सागर शाह की कमेंट्री होगी। गुकेश, जो 2024 में डिंग लिरेन को हराकर 18 साल की उम्र में 18वें विश्व चैंपियन बने, सिंधारोव के खिलाफ अपने खिताब का बचाव करेंगे, जिन्होंने 2025 FIDE विश्व कप और कैंडिडेट्स टूर्नामेंट जीतने के बाद चैंपियनशिप में अपनी जगह पक्की की। मैच में 14 शास्त्रीय खेल शामिल होंगे, जिसमें 7.5 अंक तक पहुंचने वाला पहला खिलाड़ी खिताब का दावा करेगा। -टीम स्पोर्टस्टार गोल्फ एचएसबीसी गोल्फ लीग सीजन 5 15 शहरों में 18 आयोजनों के साथ बड़ा हो गया है। एचएसबीसी इंडिया ने आज मुंबई के बॉम्बे प्रेसीडेंसी गोल्फ क्लब में एचएसबीसी गोल्फ लीग के पांचवें संस्करण का अनावरण किया, जिसने अपना अब तक का सबसे महत्वाकांक्षी कैलेंडर स्थापित किया है: 15 शहरों में 18 आयोजन, जो पिछले सीजन में 11 शहरों में 13 आयोजनों से अधिक है। पूर्व भारतीय क्रिकेटर हरभजन सिंह, 11 बार के एशियाई टूर विजेता गगनजीत भुल्लर, एशियाई खेलों की स्वर्ण पदक विजेता प्रणवी उर्स और एचएसबीसी इंडिया के जसविंदर सोढ़ी ने एचएसबीसी गोल्फ लीग के सीजन 5 का अनावरण किया। इस संस्करण का हर दौर समापन की ओर बढ़ेगा, और विजेता के लिए इनाम 2027 में 11 से 18 जुलाई के बीच सेंट एंड्रयूज में 155वें ओपन के आतिथ्य अनुभव के लिए स्कॉटलैंड की यात्रा है। एचएसबीसी इंडिया के जसविंदर सोढ़ी ने कहा, "महत्वाकांक्षा दुनिया भर में अधिक से अधिक लोगों तक गोल्फ पहुंचाना और भावी पीढ़ियों को खेल में भाग लेने के लिए प्रेरित करके सभी स्तरों पर खेल को बढ़ावा देना है, एचएसबीसी गोल्फ लीग पहले से कहीं अधिक शहरों की यात्रा करेगी, जिसका समापन गोल्फ के घर तक होगा।"

articles.contentMarathi: चेन्नई टेबल टेनिस भारताच्या 19 वर्षांखालील मुलांनी ITTF जागतिक युवा टेबल टेनिस स्पर्धेत कांस्यपदक जिंकले भारतीय मुलांच्या U-19 संघाने मंगळवारी इस्तंबूल येथे ITTF जागतिक युवा टेबल टेनिस स्पर्धेत कांस्यपदक जिंकले. भारताने उपांत्यपूर्व फेरीत तुर्कीचा 3-0 असा पराभव करून पदक निश्चित केले आणि उपांत्य फेरीत चिनी तैपेईकडून 3-0 असा पराभव पत्करावा लागला. निकाल: उपांत्यपूर्व फेरी - भारत bt तुर्की 3-0 (प्रियानुज भट्टाचार्य bt केनेन कहरामन 8-11, 11-8, 11-5; P. B. अभिनंध bt बर्क ओझटोप्राक 11-8, 6-11, 11-8, 11-6-11, Baurhammet 11-6, Baurhammet 81; 11-6, 11-9, 6-11, 11-8). उपांत्य फेरी - चायनीज तैपेई bt भारत 3-0 (चेन-येन हंग bt प्रियानुज 9-11, 11-6, 7-11, 12-10, 12-10; चिन-टिंग लिन bt P. B. अभिनंद 15-13, 11-4, 7-17, वायटी हांग; बालमुरुगन 13-11, 11-9, 11-6). -टीम स्पोर्ट्सस्टार टेनिस इंटरनॅशनल लॉन टेनिस क्लब ऑफ इंडिया 75 वा वर्धापन दिन साजरा करेल आंतरराष्ट्रीय लॉन टेनिस क्लब ऑफ इंडिया आपला 75 वा वर्धापन दिन 27 ते 29 नोव्हेंबर दरम्यान दिल्ली जिमखाना क्लब येथे 10 देशांतील खेळाडूंचा समावेश असलेला तीन दिवसीय आंतरराष्ट्रीय टेनिस मेळावा आयोजित करून साजरा करेल. 1951. 1924 मध्ये ग्रेट ब्रिटनमध्ये 102 वर्षे जुनी आंतरराष्ट्रीय लॉन टेनिस क्लब चळवळीची स्थापना टेनिसच्या माध्यमातून देशांमधील संबंध दृढ करण्याच्या कल्पनेने झाली. त्याची आता 42 देशांमध्ये उपस्थिती आहे ज्यामध्ये सुमारे 4,500 सदस्य आहेत आणि हे ब्रीदवाक्य फॉलो करते: "जाळ्यावर हस्तांदोलन आणि समुद्र ओलांडून मैत्री." अर्जेंटिना, बार्बाडोस, आयर्लंड, युनायटेड किंगडम, नॉर्वे, स्वीडन, बेल्जियम, स्लोव्हेनिया, ऑस्ट्रेलिया आणि भारत हे सहभागी देश आहेत. सहभागींमध्ये माजी खेळाडूंचा समावेश आहे, या स्पर्धेत पाच संघांचे दोन गट राऊंड-रॉबिन स्वरूपात आहेत, त्यानंतर उपांत्य फेरी आणि 29 नोव्हेंबर रोजी अंतिम फेरी होईल. भारतीय टेनिस दिग्गज आणि माजी डेव्हिस कप खेळाडू रमेश कृष्णन, ज्युनियर विम्बल्डन आणि फ्रेंच ओपन चॅम्पियन, या स्पर्धेचे उद्घाटन करतील. -पीटीआय चेस नॉडविन गेमिंग गुकेश-सिंदारोव वर्ल्ड चॅम्पियनशिप संघर्ष भारतीय चाहत्यांच्या जवळ आणण्यासाठी NODWIN गेमिंग मंगळवारपासून सुरू होणाऱ्या FIDE वर्ल्ड चॅम्पियनशिप 2026 च्या FIDE वर्ल्ड चॅम्पियनशिपच्या हिंदी प्रसारणास समर्थन देण्यासाठी सज्ज आहे. भारतातील दर्शक 14-गेम स्पर्धेचे हिंदी प्रसारणाद्वारे आणि हॅबिटॅट, मुंबई येथे थेट पाहण्याचा अनुभव घेण्यास सक्षम असतील. प्रसारणासोबतच, हॅबिटॅट लाइव्ह पाहण्याचा अनुभव होस्ट करेल जिथे चाहते 2024 वर्ल्ड चॅम्पियनशिप दरम्यान अशाच मेळाव्याच्या आधारावर चॅम्पियनशिप एकत्र फॉलो करू शकतात. चेस डॉट कॉम इंडियाच्या सहकार्याने NODWIN गेमिंगच्या YouTube चॅनेलवर पाहण्याचा अनुभव प्रसारित केला जाईल, ज्यामध्ये तानिया सचदेव, अमृता मोकल, हर्षित राजा, साहिल टिकू, सहज ग्रोव्हर आणि सागर शाह यांच्या समालोचनाचा समावेश आहे. डिंग लिरेनचा पराभव करून वयाच्या 18 व्या वर्षी 2024 मध्ये 18 वा विश्वविजेता बनलेला गुकेश, 2025 FIDE विश्वचषक आणि उमेदवार स्पर्धा जिंकून articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes fastest hundred and double century in List A cricket during India A's victory over UAE - Sky Sports
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi smashes fastest hundred and double century in List A cricket during India A's victory over UAE Sky Sports
articles.content: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has broken more records as the teenage cricket sensation smashed his way to the fastest century and double century in List A cricket during India A's seven-wicket victory against the United Arab Emirates on Tuesday. The 15-year-old produced an extraordinary innings, making 204 off a mere 53 deliveries, including 28 sixes, during the Asia Cup Rising Stars group match in Doha. Sooryavanshi, who became the youngest debutant for India's senior T20 side in July , first raced his way to a 28-ball century, the fastest ton hit in List A cricket, surpassing Jake Fraser-McGurk by one delivery. Sooryavanshi becomes youngest player to debut for India Who are Sooryavanshi's rivals for world's best T20 opener? Listen to latest episode of the Sky Sports Cricket Podcast The Indian prodigy then went one better, advancing to his second ton off 24 balls to obliterate the record, previously held by Chad Bowes, for the fastest double century struck in List A cricket [103 balls]. His 40-ball 150 was also the fastest in List A cricket too, with the 15-year-old going on to smash four consecutive sixes. It came after UAE had set India a target of 250 to win and thanks to Sooryavanshi's feats, Tilak Varma's side would go on to seal victory inside 14.2 overs. Sooryavanshi completed the feat by smashing an incredible 28 sixes and seven fours, with a strike rate of 384.90. That surpassed Western Australia's D'Arcy Short's record tally of 23 maximums, which he managed during a match against Queensland in 2019. Known as a ruthless ball striker, Sooryavanshi was named the IPL's MVP for the 2026 season, after leading the league with 776 runs and a strike rate of 237.30. In February, he set a new record for the highest score made at an Under-19 Cricket World Cup final, making 175 runs from 80 deliveries, as India went on to seal a 100-run win against England. Sooryavanshi would ultimately be dismissed in the 13th over after he clipped a delivery from Basil Hameed to Aryansh Sharma at long-off.

articles.title: Meet Shodhan Rai: The 45-Year-Old Indian Who Keeps Finishing Second Best in the World - Open Magazine
articles.summary: Meet Shodhan Rai: The 45-Year-Old Indian Who Keeps Finishing Second Best in the World Open Magazine
articles.content: Look at the photograph first. A man stands in front of a black-and-gold wall that reads The Pinnacle of Natural Sports. His arms are stretched high above his head, holding the Indian flag at full width. The shoulders rise into two hard, rounded caps. The arms are thick with muscle, veins running down the forearms. Below the ribs, the abdomen is cut into deep, separate blocks. The thighs are carved into long, visible lines. Pinned to his trunks is a number: 155. Round his neck hangs a medal. He is 45 years old. He is smiling. The flag is creased and marked, like something that has travelled a long way. So has he. Shodhan Rai has represented India in 39 international competitions, his team says. And the medal is silver. Again. "I had set my sights on winning gold this year," he said after the 2026 Natural Olympia, the biggest stage in natural bodybuilding. It was his ninth medal there: two silvers and six bronzes before this one, according to his team. Ten years after his first Olympia silver, gold is still one step above him. By his team's count in 2025, he had reached the podium in 35 of his 36 international tournaments. Almost always among the best. Never, in Las Vegas, the best. The body in that photograph looks like victory. The life behind it tells a different story. THE FIRST BODY HE EVER STUDIED Those arms began with another man's arms. The first bodybuilder Shodhan Rai ever watched closely was his father, J.N. Rai, a well-known Karnataka bodybuilder whom his son calls his inspiration and first guru. He introduced the boy to the sport at ten. At sixteen, during school breaks, Shodhan was put on a full training routine. At seventeen he stood on a state stage for the first time. The father passed on more than a sport. He passed on a way of doing it. Shodhan has always credited his father for his love of bodybuilding "the natural way", in a sport, as one Deccan Chronicle writer put it, that is often seen as an abused one. In 2001, still under 21, he went to Charnay-lès-Mâcon in France for the Mr Universe and came home with a bronze. In 2014 Karnataka gave him the Ekalavya Award for 2013, the state's highest sporting honour. By then he had begun to learn the other lesson of his profession. Medals at home, and honours from the state, do not pay for the next flight out. THE PRICE OF A FLIGHT Look at the abdomen in the photograph again. Every one of those blocks has a bill attached. In December 2022, back in Bengaluru, Rai did the arithmetic for Kannada Prabha. A single international contest, with flights, hotel, entry fees and food, cost him about ₹4–5 lakh. Between June and November there were five or six prestigious international meets. With the money he had, he could afford one or two. That year he had just come back from America with two very different verdicts. At the Natural World Cup in Los Angeles, he won gold in the over-35 category. At the Natural Olympia in Las Vegas, the same body finished seventh. This is the arithmetic of a sport without patrons. In a country that pours its money and its love into cricket, a man who has represented India 39 times still has to ask for help. In June 2025, already in the Hall of Fame, he asked in public. "Natural Bodybuilding is an expensive affair," he said. He was looking for "crucial support from sports promoters around the world with endorsements and sports sponsorships that will help me sustain and continue the journey to the top." After Las Vegas this year, his team made the same appeal again. So he pays for it the way he always has. With his hands. Rai is an internationally certified fitness consultant. His team says he has advised several high-profile clients, among them Zerodha co-founder Nikhil Kamath, whom Forbes valued at $3.3 billion last December. Sit with that for a moment. The hands that help shape a billionaire's body belong to a man still looking for someone to pay for his flights. He has never pretended the balance is easy. "I do fitness consulting too, but bodybuilding is my priority," he said in 2017. And: "You can have an alternate career but not a taxing and time consuming one." The day job has to pay for everything. It just cannot be allowed to cost him the body. THE LONG WAY ROUND There is a faster way to build a body like that. Rai has spent three decades refusing it. He competes only in tested, natural bodybuilding. The belief that a body like his cannot be built without steroids or shortcuts is, he once said, "the BIGGEST MYTH!" This month he put it more quietly. "Staying being natural and competing naturally over all these years has been the key for sustaining for so long." The choice that made his road slower is also the reason he is still on it at 45. The natural road is slow. "Bodybuilding takes a long time to show results," he has said. His own record shows it. At the Natural Olympia in Reno in 2012, he finished fifth. At San Diego in 2013, eighth. In 2014, sixth. Year after year, he flew halfway around the world to be told he was good, but not good enough. Then, in 2016, in Las Vegas, the gap closed to one man. Silver. And 2017 became the year of his life. Gold at the Natural Mr India. Gold at the Natural Universe in Auckland. Gold at the Natural World Cup. Bronze at the Natural Olympia. "The year 2017 has been the best year of my career so far in natural bodybuilding," he said. "The standard of athletes was top notch and every year, the standard got even better." That last line was a warning. Every year the field got better. Every year, he got older. And then the world champion did something telling. He went home to prepare for Mr Karnataka. "I always like to compete here since the best athletes from Karnataka get on stage every year," he said. "It is also a platform for the state team selections." Gold in Auckland and Los Angeles, and he still wanted to earn his place in the state team. THE SHOULDERS THE JUDGES DOUBTED Now look at the shoulders. They are the first thing you see in the photograph: two broad, rounded caps, rising above a tricolour stretched to full width. articles.title: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits 52-ball double century, 28 sixes in world record knock - India Today
articles.summary: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi hits 52-ball double century, 28 sixes in world record knock India Today
articles.content: Brief Score: India A (254 for 3 in 14.2 overs) beat UAE (2498 in 50 overs) by 7 wickets in the Rising Stars Asia Cup match in Doha. Vaibhav Sooryavanshi (204 in 53 balls). Vaibhav Sooryavanshi spent Tuesday breaking one world record after another in Doha. The 15-year-old smashed a 28-ball century, followed it up with a 52-ball double hundred and hit a record 28 sixes, rewriting the record books in List A cricket. He finished with a breathtaking 204 off just 53 deliveries, powering India A to a record chase of 250 against the UAE in the Rising Stars Asia Cup on Tuesday, November 24, on the occasion of Guru Purab. IND A vs UAE HighlightsIndia chased down the target in just 14.2 overs, sealing a seven-wicket win on the back of Sooryavanshi's breathtaking 204 off 53 balls. In a staggering display of power-hitting, 28 of the 53 deliveries he faced sailed over the boundary for six.Sooryavanshi's double century, which came off just 52 balls, was the fastest in 50-over cricket, comfortably surpassing the previous record held by New Zealand's Chad Bowes. Bowes had scored a double hundred off 103 deliveries for Canterbury against Otago in New Zealand's domestic 50-over competition in October 2024.The teenager also set a new world record for the most sixes in a List A innings, smashing 28 to go past the previous mark of 23 held by Australia's D'Arcy Short.Earlier, Sooryavanshi had broken Fraser-McGurk's record for the fastest century in List A cricket. The Australian had scored a 29-ball hundred for South Australia against Tasmania in October 2023. Sooryavanshi bettered that mark by a delivery, reaching his century in just 28 balls.Sooryavanshi played down the significance of the record, saying he was determined to make a big score after having had trouble to convert his starts in the first two matches of the Rising Stars Asia Cup 2026 edition."In the last two matches, I got set but couldn't convert those starts. So the plan was to go out there and take my time initially. But after facing a ball or two, I felt the bowlers weren't getting much help from the surface, so I backed my strengths," he said.Sooryavanshi was dismissed for 26 against Nepal on November 20. He made 11 against Pakistan Shaheens on Sunday. Sooryavanshi showed no signs of slowing down at the University of Doha for Science and Technology, taking on spinners and pacers with equal contempt and sending the ball soaring over the boundary with remarkable regularity.It was the second time Sooryavanshi had crossed the 150-run mark in List A cricket. He had earlier smashed a 36-ball century before going on to score 190 off 84 deliveries for Bihar against Arunachal Pradesh in the 2025-26 Vijay Hazare Trophy, India's domestic 50-over competition.FASTEST CENTURIES IN LIST A CRICKET28 balls - Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, India A vs UAE (2026)29 balls - Jake Fraser-McGurk, South Australia vs Tasmania (2023)31 balls - AB de Villiers, South Africa vs West Indies (2015)32 balls - Sakibul Gani, Bihar vs Arunachal Pradesh (2025)Breaking records is fast becoming a habit for Sooryavanshi. In his maiden IPL season, he smashed a 35-ball century for Rajasthan Royals against Gujarat Titans, setting the record for the fastest century by an Indian batter in the tournament. He also became the youngest player to score an IPL hundred.Tuesday's knock was another display of extraordinary audacity and self-belief. Sooryavanshi went after the bowlers from the very first over, taking on the UAE attack with an astonishing appetite for big hits.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi said he might wait until the end of the tournament to celebrate his double century. But back home in Samastipur, Bihar, his family members were celebrating the landmark with crackers and cake. Sooryavanshi's family in his village, Samastipur, celebrated the landmark double hundred with a cake (India Today Photo)SOORYAVANSHI'S DOUBLE HUNDRED IN POINTERSThe carnage began in the very first over of India's chase. Sooryavanshi took on fast bowler Zahid Ali, launching him for three sixes to make his intentions clear.There was no let-up in the second over. Facing Ibrar Ahmed, the teenager cleared the ropes twice more. By the end of the third over, Sooryavanshi had raced to his fifty off just 15 balls, taking his sixes tally to seven.The onslaught continued even after India lost opening partner Abhishek Sharma, who was dismissed by Ibrar in the fourth over. Sooryavanshi responded in stunning fashion, launching the bowler over the boundary with a pull shot off the second delivery after the dismissal.India's 100 came up in just the fifth over, with Sooryavanshi already on 82 off 23 deliveries. He brought up his century in the seventh over, reaching the landmark with a powerful straight drive against Ibrar.The sixes kept coming. Left-arm spinner Uddish Suri was the next to feel the heat as Sooryavanshi smashed three sixes in a single over. By the end of the 10th over, India had raced to 183 for 2, while the teenager had brought up his 150 off just 40 balls. India's total was the highest by any team at the end of 10 overs in a List A match.There was still more to come. Sooryavanshi took 28 runs off the 12th over, including four sixes, as he closed in on a scarcely believable double century. He reached the 200-run mark off just 52 balls, bringing up the milestone with a six.His extraordinary innings finally came to an end in the 13th over when he attempted to clear long-on off Basil Hameed but found a fielder. By then, however, the damage had been done. Sooryavanshi walked back after scoring 204 off just 53 deliveries, having put India firmly on course for victory.India completed a massive seven-wicket win, sealing their place in the semi-finals of the Rising Stars Asia Cup.- Ends

articles.title: Sharad Pawar seeks Maharashtra CM post for Supriya Sule amid alleged talks with BJP for NDA entry - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Sharad Pawar seeks Maharashtra CM post for Supriya Sule amid alleged talks with BJP for NDA entry The New Indian Express
articles.content: MUMABAI: Sharad Pawar is reportedly negotiating a possible political realignment with the BJP, with sources claiming that the veteran NCP leader has sought the Maharashtra Chief Minister’s post for his daughter, Lok Sabha MP Supriya Sule, in return for backing the BJP-led NDA’s proposed delimitation and women’s reservation legislation and joining the alliance.Highly placed sources claim that backchannel negotiations are taking place directly between Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union Home Minister Amit Shah and Sharad Pawar.The BJP is reportedly keen to secure the numbers needed to pass the proposed delimitation and women's reservation bills, which failed to clear Parliament in their earlier attempt, and is seeking a two-thirds majority in both Houses.According to a source familiar with the negotiations, the BJP initially offered Supriya Sule a key Cabinet portfolio, but Sharad Pawar reportedly sought the Chief Minister’s post for her instead.In return, he is said to have offered to mobilise smaller parties in support of the proposed legislation and is reportedly in touch with some Congress MPs unhappy with their leadership who could consider remaining absent during voting.The discussions are also reportedly linked to efforts to reunite the two NCP factions. A senior NCP leader involved in the negotiations claimed that the BJP had earlier tried to persuade NCP national president Sunetra Pawar to agree to a merger, but she remained reluctant..The leader said the BJP was now exploring an alternative arrangement by offering significant political space to the Sharad Pawar-led NCP (SP) in the Maharashtra government. The proposed arrangement could include the Finance portfolio and, if the Chief Minister's post were also conceded, could force Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth to reconsider their position, accept Sharad Pawar's leadership or move away from the government.Several senior NCP leaders are reportedly in favour of Sharad Pawar taking charge of both factions and securing a larger role in the state government, amid concerns among party legislators over their political future.Meanwhile, the NCP (SP) leadership has reportedly advised its district-level functionaries against directly targeting the BJP and its senior leaders, while asking them to continue raising public issues.Farmers affected by drought had planned a march under MLA Rohit Pawar's leadership from December 7 to 9 during the winter session of the Maharashtra legislature. However, the party's senior leadership reportedly contacted district presidents and asked them to refrain from organising the agitation against the BJP-led government, with leaders said to be wary of jeopardising the ongoing negotiations."Talks are underway, but it is difficult to say whether they will translate into a concrete arrangement. Sharad Pawar is known for keeping his political options open and can change his decisions at the last moment. The BJP is keen to bring him into the NDA, but nothing can be taken for granted until an official announcement is made," a senior NCP (SP) leader said.

articles.summary: IFFI 2026: Maharashtra Government plans new push for global film collaborations and independent cinema – MovieTalkies
articles.content: IFFI 2026 Maharashtra Government Global Push For Low Budget Cinema: The Maharashtra government is planning to introduce a dedicated mechanism to encourage international film co-productions and help independent films reach wider audiences. The proposed initiatives aim to strengthen the state's film ecosystem and make Maharashtra a more attractive destination for domestic as well as international filmmakers. Sara Tendulkar and Rajveer Deol getting married? Here's the truth – The plans were discussed by Dr. Kiran Kulkarni, Secretary of the Cultural Affairs Department, Government of Maharashtra, during a panel discussion at the 57th International Film Festival of India – IFFI 2026 – in Goa today. Organised by the Maharashtra Film, Stage and Cultural Development Corporation at the Waves Film Bazaar , the session focused on the future opportunities and growth of Maharashtra's cultural and film industries. The panel included filmmaker Nikhil Mahajan, cinematographer-director Mahesh Limaye , filmmaker-producer Suhrud Godbole and Prashant Sajanikar, Joint Managing Director of the Corporation. Film scholar and director Dr. Santosh Pathare moderated the discussion. During the session, Kulkarni said the state government would work towards setting up an institutional framework through the Corporation to make international film collaborations easier. The proposal came after Nikhil Mahajan pointed out the increasing interest among foreign production houses in working with Indian filmmakers. A structured mechanism could help Marathi and other Indian-language films find international partners, explore new markets and build cross-border creative collaborations. Kulkarni also highlighted Maharashtra's single-window clearance system for film shoots, which aims to provide permissions from different government departments within seven days. Around 5,000 permissions for outdoor shooting locations have already been issued through this system, making it easier for production houses to shoot across the state. Another important subject discussed was the difficulty faced by independent filmmakers in securing theatrical releases. High multiplex ticket prices, limited screenings and inconvenient show timings often restrict the reach of smaller films. Kulkarni said the government was exploring technology-based solutions to improve theatrical access and help low-budget films connect with more viewers. Discussions with the concerned departments are also underway. Prashant Sajanikar stressed that developing a strong film ecosystem requires more than infrastructure, adding that the Corporation is engaging with filmmakers to understand their changing requirements and address industry challenges. Mahesh Limaye highlighted Maharashtra's diverse shooting locations and production facilities while emphasising the importance of maintaining them responsibly. He urged production teams to restore locations after shoots so that other filmmakers could continue using them. Meanwhile, Suhrud Godbole welcomed efforts to take emerging Marathi filmmakers to international festivals such as Cannes . He noted that global exposure can help young directors develop professional connections, understand international filmmaking practices and explore future collaborations.
